# Product Discovery
Guide product discovery processes — user research, problem validation, opportunity sizing, and hypothesis testing.
## When to Activate
- Starting a new product initiative - Validating a feature idea - Exploring a new market opportunity - User research and persona development - Defining product-market fit hypotheses
## Key Frameworks
- Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD) - Opportunity Solution Tree - Lean Canvas - User Story Mapping - Design Thinking
## Deliverables
- Problem statement - User personas - Opportunity assessment - Hypothesis backlog - Discovery findings report

PRD Writing
pm-prd-writing

# PRD Writing
Write clear, actionable Product Requirement Documents.
## PRD Structure
1. Problem Statement 2. User Stories (with acceptance criteria) 3. Success Metrics 4. Technical Considerations 5. Dependencies 6. Open Questions 7. Timeline Estimate
## Writing Guidelines
- Start with the problem, not the solution - Use INVEST criteria for user stories - Define measurable success metrics - Include edge cases and error states

Effectively manage product stakeholders through structured communication and engagement.
## Key Tools
- RACI Matrix - Stakeholder Map (influence vs. interest) - Communication Plan - Escalation Paths - Decision Log
## Best Practices
- Over-communicate to key stakeholders - Document decisions with rationale - Run regular steering committee updates - Maintain a risk and issue register

Sprint Planning

# Sprint Planning
Facilitate effective sprint planning sessions.
## Sprint Planning Agenda
1. Review sprint goal and capacity 2. Refine top backlog items 3. Estimate effort (story points, t-shirt sizes) 4. Commit to sprint scope 5. Define sprint goal
## Key Metrics
- Team velocity (last 3-5 sprints average) - Capacity (accounting for holidays, PTO) - Carry-over from previous sprint

User Story Mapping
pm-user-story-mapping

# User Story Mapping
Create visual maps of the user journey to plan releases and prioritize work.
## Story Mapping Process
1. Define the user's journey (backbone) 2. Break down into activities and tasks 3. Prioritize vertically (must-have → nice-to-have) 4. Slice horizontally into releases 5. Identify MVP scope
## Deliverables
- Story map (visual) - Release plan - MVP definition

# User Story Mapping

Prioritization
pm-prioritization
Prioritize features — RICE, ICE, MoSCoW, Kano model, value vs effort, cost of delay

# Prioritization
Apply structured frameworks to prioritize features and initiatives.
## Frameworks
- **RICE**: Reach × Impact × Confidence ÷ Effort - **ICE**: Impact × Confidence × Ease - **MoSCoW**: Must / Should / Could / Won't - **Kano Model**: Basic / Performance / Delighter - **Cost of Delay**: Value lost per time unit
## When to Use Each
- RICE: Data-driven, quantifiable decisions - MoSCoW: Fixed-scope releases - Kano: Feature satisfaction analysis - Cost of Delay: Time-sensitive opportunities

# Prioritization
Apply structured frameworks to prioritize features and initiatives.
Retrospectives
pm-retrospectives
Facilitate retrospectives — start/stop/continue, 4Ls, sailboat, action item tracking

# Retrospectives
Facilitate effective retrospectives that drive continuous improvement.
## Retrospective Formats
- **Start / Stop / Continue**: Simple, actionable - **4Ls**: Liked / Learned / Lacked / Longed for - **Sailboat**: What propelled us / What held us back - **Mad / Sad / Glad**: Emotion-focused
## Facilitation Tips
- Set the stage with check-in - Gather data before generating insights - Vote on top action items - Assign owners to each action - Review previous actions at start

# Retrospectives
Facilitate effective retrospectives that drive continuous improvement.
Agile Metrics
pm-agile-metrics
Track agile metrics — burndown, burnup, velocity, cycle time, lead time, CFD, throughput

# Agile Metrics
Track and interpret agile metrics to improve team performance and predictability.
## Key Metrics
- **Burndown/Burnup**: Sprint progress tracking - **Velocity**: Story points completed per sprint - **Cycle Time**: Time from start to done per item - **Lead Time**: Time from request to delivery - **Cumulative Flow Diagram (CFD)**: WIP and bottlenecks - **Throughput**: Items completed per time period
## Interpretation
- Declining velocity → investigate blockers - Increasing cycle time → check WIP limits - CFD flatlining → bottleneck at specific stage - High variance → improve estimation or break down stories

# Agile Metrics
Track and interpret agile metrics to improve team performance and predictability.
